Suggested approaches included interviewing designers, fabric suppliers, textile manufacturers, and retailers; attending trade shows and conferences; collaborating on research projects; and contributing findings to industry publications.

Potential challenges for research assistants collaborating with fashion-industry professionals on textile research include professionals’ limited time, restricted access to confidential company information, limited research funding, differing priorities (such as design, cost, and productivity versus sustainability), and language or communication barriers.

Suggested strategies for overcoming textile-research collaboration challenges included setting clear expectations and timelines, scheduling meetings in advance, building trust and sharing findings, seeking grants, sponsors, or industry partnerships, identifying shared priorities such as sustainability and ethical production, communicating clearly and requesting feedback, and using translation services or bilingual collaborators where needed.

Potential benefits of research-assistant textile research for the fashion industry include developing innovative materials, identifying more sustainable materials and production methods, improving product durability and wearability, addressing waste and production-efficiency challenges, and helping companies understand consumer preferences and respond to changing trends.
